rows: The `afkv2-note v1` format text `NOTE-FORMAT.md` and its parser `dogfood_note.py`: `parse(text)` reads a note, and `check(note, worktrees)` returns each failure with its rule code, its place and its reason, for the 10 rule codes.
The note format and its parser are 1 contract between the 2 agents, so the text and the code that checks it are cut together and come first.

The core of `dogfood.py`: `main(argv, env, runner)`, the JSON answer and exit codes, the versioned state file, the caller guard on `HERDR_PANE_ID`, and the verbs `start` and `status`. `start` opens 1 pane, starts the afkv2 agent with its model, effort and auto-approval, and sends the role and the ask; a live state forwards the ask instead. It also writes the in-process fake runner that later subtasks reuse.
Every verb needs the state file, the caller guard and the JSON answer; start builds them, so it comes before the other verbs.

The 2 verbs only the afkv2 pane may call: `worktree` makes the small-asks worktree or a medium worktree from the confirmed base; `note` checks a note, stores it in the notes folder, types a 1-line pointer into the main pane and records it.
worktree and note are the 2 verbs only the afkv2 pane calls; note needs the parser of 0001.

The verbs only the main pane may call: `tell` sends feedback or the wrap request to the afkv2 agent; `check-note` parses a received note and writes nothing; `close` ends the session after the wrap report and keeps every worktree and branch. It closes the guard check across all 7 verbs.
tell, check-note and close are the main-pane verbs; with them all 7 verbs exist, so the guard test across every verb lives here.

`setup.py source [--path P]` suggests a likely plugin source checkout, or writes the `source <path>` line of the install record after its checks; `status` gains the field `source`; setup SKILL.md gains the step that asks only when the line is missing or broken.
The setup change is its own module in an existing skill and needs nothing of dogfood, so it can build in any order.
`SKILL.md` of `/afkv2:dogfood`, read by the main agent: the refusals and their repairs, the start, the 1 exception to playbook rule H-8, the pointer to APPLY.md, feedback, and the wrap-up.
The main agent's skill text runs its command blocks against the finished dogfood.py, so it waits for every verb.

`AGENT.md`, the role the afkv2 agent reads from its worktree: the branch question, the lanes, the queue, the note and the wrap. `APPLY.md`, how the main agent applies each change kind CK-1 to CK-4 and redoes a named delta.
AGENT.md and APPLY.md share 1 static check and point at the note format and the worktree verb.

The high-level tests of the start and the setup step: the command-line refusals as child processes, and a live script that drives real herdr panes with real Claude and Codex main agents, 1 row per run, with a recorded result.
High-level tests of the start, the refusals and setup, in real herdr panes; a test subtask owns no low-level row.
